title: High-value property tax could rise beyond 2028 rates
summary:
The High Value Council Tax Surcharge may increase beyond its initial 2028 rates as the government seeks to fund spending commitments, according to Knight Frank. The annual surcharge, ranging from £2,500 to £7,400 on properties worth £2 million or more, was announced in last autumn's Budget.

title: Half of UK property markets see longer selling times
summary:
Properties in half of Britain's local markets are taking longer to sell compared to the same period last year, according to analysis from Zoopla, despite national average selling times remaining static. While the national average time to sell stands at 42 days, unchanged year-on-year to July 2026, the property portal's research identified 180 of the 363 local authorities across England, Scotland and Wales where selling times have increased over the past 12 months.

title: Strettons appoints Olivia Boulting as auction director
summary:
London property firm Strettons has appointed Olivia Boulting as director and auctioneer in a newly created role designed to expand the company's auction operations. Boulting joins from Auction House UK where she managed teams across offices in Bristol, Devon and Cornwall.

title: Estate agencies face £45,000 annual AML compliance costs
summary:
Estate agencies in the UK may need to allocate approximately £45,000 annually for a dedicated compliance officer to meet anti-money laundering obligations, according to analysis by property technology firm Coadjute. The estimate follows HMRC's updated AML guidance requiring risk-based approaches to preventing money laundering.

title: Government fast-tracks housing near transport hubs
summary:
The government has announced planning reforms that will fast-track approval for thousands of new homes near public transport stations across England. Industry bodies have welcomed improved transport access but warned against creating fragmented developments.

title: Industry renews pressure for Help to Buy scheme revival
summary:
The Home Builders Federation has renewed calls for the government to reintroduce the Help to Buy Equity Loan Scheme, citing record-low planning approvals and suppressed demand in the new-build market. The scheme, which operated between 2013 and 2022, generated a £1.24 billion return for the Treasury.

title: MERA closes £1.63m development exit loan in Dalston
summary:
MERA Investment Management has completed a £1,627,500 development exit facility for a developer refinancing a three-bedroom house and commercial unit in Dalston, East London. The transaction was completed in four weeks with 75% LTV on residential and 70% on commercial elements.

title: Solar households earn £100m selling power to grid
summary:
More than 400,000 British households have collectively earned almost £100 million over the past year by exporting surplus solar electricity to the grid through Octopus Energy's export tariff schemes. According to data released by the energy supplier, customers received an average payment of £244 during the 12-month period.

title: Land Registry and Ordnance Survey sign data partnership
summary:
HM Land Registry and Ordnance Survey have signed a three-year partnership to improve data connectivity across England and Wales' £9 trillion property market. The collaboration supports government targets to deliver 1.5 million new homes while reducing transaction friction.

title: UK property sales agreed drop 11% in single week
summary:
The UK property market recorded an 11% weekly decline in sales agreed during the week ending 9 August 2026, with 21,800 homes sold subject to contract. The sharp drop follows two consecutive weeks of stronger-than-expected activity that had bucked normal seasonal trends.
